visual_source_files.evidence: README/project asset has the exact paper title and author metadata; the 4,366×1,683 image matches the PDF Figure 1 schematic content and layout, while the PDF embeds an internal fig/schematic.pdf Form.

Cells 3, 5, 6, and 8 contain the latent time-series, metric/trajectory, sub-connectivity, and permutation-complexity plotting code corresponding to Figures 2, 8, and 9; paper method labels FacRNN where the notebook uses DisRNN.

Cells 1–2 generate the two rank-3 Lorenz/Thomas groups and cells 8/15 create pairplot/KDE views; cell 2 specifies the 3D trajectory line width. These cells explain Figure 5, whose final PDF rendering is one raster image.

Cells 6–13 define thresholded positive/negative chord diagrams, M1 trajectory grids, and rotation curves corresponding to Figure 3; the public tree contains no compiled fig/monkey.pdf or monkey_conn.pdf.

source_acquisition.search_note: The PDF p.9 Software and Data link explicitly names https://github.com/JerrySoybean/facrnn. gh metadata and README title/author/paper links match the paper exactly, and the recursive tree was inspected read-only. The local visual-source candidate visualization.ipynb is actually an ISO MP4 (ftypisom) byte-identical to voltage.mp4, so it is excluded. The public tree has no paper TeX, fig/ PDFs, Figure 4/6/7/10 plot source, or Table 1 generator; internal PTEX filenames are not public source paths. The resulting status is partial_visual_source, not exact_visual_source.

paper_style.palette_strategy: The paper mixes Matplotlib categorical method colors (Figures 2 and 8), direction colors (Figure 3), and red/blue signed-value maps or edges (Figures 4 and 10). There is no cross-figure color dictionary, so the same hue can carry different semantics.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Most diagrams, trajectories, tables, and labels are vector PDF content. Raster content is concentrated in Figure 2/4 tile maps, the full Figure 5 image, Figure 9 complexity raster, and Figure 10 matrix tiles.
paper_style.style_consistency: The main/appendix objects share compact page-width compositions and sans-serif figure labels, but imported vector fonts, Type3 DejaVu Sans, KaTeX/Computer Modern math, and Nimbus Roman table text create a mixed typography contract. Appendix multi-panel figures are denser and smaller than main figures.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1. (a): Schematic of the FacRNN, showing independent latent groups and the corresponding low-rank connectivities. (b): Group-wise independence: (z₁, z₂) ⊥ (z₃, z₄), while within-groups are highly entangled, and components from different groups are marginally independent.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue and orange identify latent groups; green marks KDE structure; red marks sample points; black and gray carry equations, arrows, and axes.

encodings.color: blue/orange group blocks, green KDE, and red sample points
encodings.text: group labels, equations, component labels, and panel letters

figures.data_and_statistics: A conceptual object rather than a sampled estimate: panel (b) depicts K=4 components in G=2 groups with within-group dependence and cross-group marginal independence. The diagram contains no sample size, confidence interval, or fitted statistic.
figures.evidence_relation: PDF p.4 connects the observation-to-latent-to-decoder pipeline, the group factorization, and W=AB/W=ΣW_g interpretation in §3; Figure 2–4 instantiate the interface on synthetic, M1, and mouse data.
design_strengths: It binds the encoder/decoder, independent groups, and low-rank sub-connectivity into one causal visual chain.
The companion independence panel makes the intended group-wise versus within-group dependence distinction visible.
design_weaknesses: Formulae, 3D insets, KDE contours, and arrows compete for a small page-width canvas.
Small type and pale fills weaken group-color discrimination under scaling or grayscale printing; the caption does not decode every color.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use one end-to-end schematic to bind a model interface, its structural assumption, and the interpretable output decomposition before quantitative panels.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2. (a): The PC and R² of the estimated latent, and the connectivity correlation. The starbars indicate the pairwise t-test significance levels. Arrows indicate the higher or lower the better. (b): Group 2 latent trajectories with the true dynamics in 3D plots; and the 1D trajectories from different methods on selected latent components. All latent dimensions are plotted in Fig. 8 in Appendix A.3.1. (c): The learned sub-connectivities from different methods and the ground truth.

color.semantic_mapping: Method identity uses the Matplotlib categorical sequence; black is true dynamics; the seismic matrix scale maps negative/near-zero/positive connectivity to blue/white/red.

figures.evidence_relation: PDF p.6 §4.1 uses the three-part object for the synthetic comparison: metrics first, representative latent dynamics second, and learned versus ground-truth sub-connectivities third. The caption points to Figure 8 for all six latent dimensions.
design_strengths: It closes a metric-to-dynamics-to-structure loop in one traceable object.
The shared method legend lets distributions, trajectories, and matrices be read as the same comparison.

The caption does not define boxplot spread, mean markers, matrix color bounds, or matrix units in enough detail for independent decoding.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3. (a): Recovered latent trajectories from different methods v.s. the ground-truth trajectories, and their alignment R² scores. (b): The corresponding low-rank connectivity for K = 2 FacRNN and K = 4 FacRNN. For FacRNN, for example, the rank-4 connectivity can be decomposed into two rank-2 sub-connectivities, one responsible for the dynamics of the x-movement, and the other for the y-movement. Panel (a) reports alignment R² summaries; panel (b) thresholds A@B connectivity to show signed edges and additive rank-2 pieces; panel (c) plots alignment R² over rotation angle with a shaded band whose aggregation is not defined in the caption.
figures.evidence_relation: PDF p.7 §4.2 links hand-coordinate alignment, rank-1 failure, rank-2/rank-4 decomposition, and coordinate-rotation stress testing. The public conv.ipynb reproduces the trajectory/chord/rotation plotting logic, while Figure 10 expands the connectivity matrices.
design_strengths: It puts task alignment, interpretable connectivity decomposition, and coordinate robustness on one page.
The additive rank-4 = rank-2 x-movement + rank-2 y-movement relation is visually explicit.
design_weaknesses: Many small multiples and chord diagrams leave no room for a sign legend or shared trajectory scale.
The rotation band lacks a stated statistical definition, and method names differ between the public notebook (DisRNN) and the paper (FacRNN).
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair representative trajectories with additive sub-connectivity networks and a rotation curve to test appearance, mechanism, and coordinate robustness separately.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1. Monkey M1 β ablation. Values are mean (std) across five runs.

tables.uncertainty: Each cell reports mean (std) across five runs, as stated in the caption; no interval or significance marker is shown.
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows use β values 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, and 200. Recon. log-likelihood is approximately 379.422–380.001 while Between-group PC falls from about 0.0165 to 0.000220. Decimal places vary by column and no unit or held-out split is reported.
tables.evidence_relation: PDF p.16 A.3.2 uses the table to select a real-data β interval by contrasting reconstruction with between-group PC; it supplies hyperparameter context for Figure 3 and Figure 10 and parallels the synthetic sweep in Figure 6.
design_strengths: The same β rows expose the reconstruction/structural-penalty trade-off.
Mean(std) over five runs retains repeatability information without adding a separate panel.
design_weaknesses: Column precision is inconsistent and no unit/direction is encoded in the headers.
The text-recommended β=10–20 range is not highlighted, so the selection depends on prose above the table.
tables.reusable_pattern: Report task quality and structural constraint metrics on the same regularization grid with repeated-run mean(std), then visibly mark the selected operating range.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 defines FacRNN group factorization and sub-connectivity; Figures 2–4 move through synthetic metrics/trajectories/matrices, M1 alignment/decomposition/rotation, and mouse event/capacity/spatial-temporal-network evidence. Figures 5–10 and Table 1 then supply synthetic ground truth, beta choice, alignment details, full latent traces, permutation complexity, full M1 matrices, and real-data beta evidence.
cross_object_system.caption_system: All objects use Figure n./Table 1. prefixes. Multi-panel main captions use (a)/(b)/(c) keys and Figure 2/3 provide the strongest comparison and mechanism narration, while Figures 5/6/8 and Figure 10 omit important scale, uncertainty, or encoding definitions.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: The only table uses one header row, three right-aligned metric columns, no grouped headers, and booktabs rules. It names beta, reconstruction log-likelihood, and between-group PC, but omits units, metric direction, and the selected range.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: The Figure 1 PC/group mechanism is instantiated in Figures 2–4; Figure 6 and Table 1 test beta choices, Figure 7 exposes matching, Figure 9 tests permutation cost, and Figures 8/10 expand the latent/connectivity results.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Figure 2 points to Figure 8 for all latent dimensions, Figure 3 and the p.16 text point to Figure 10 for full matrices, and short Appendix A.3 pointers lead to Figures 5–9 and Table 1 for data generation, ablation, alignment, and search-cost detail.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Figure internals predominantly use DejaVu Sans/Helvetica with KaTeX or Computer Modern math, while Table 1 follows Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern body text. This is locally coherent but lacks a single font-size/weight contract across imported vector, Type3, and raster objects.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Figures 2 and 8 share a method palette; Figure 3 reuses C0–C7 for movement direction; Figures 4 and 10 use red/blue for signed activity/connectivity; Figure 4 also uses purple/red for sweeps. Color semantics are therefore panel-local rather than globally stable.

most_reusable_patterns: Put structural assumptions, training interface, and interpretable outputs in one schematic before quantitative evidence.
Use the Figure 2 statistics → representative trajectory → structural matrix sequence to close a metric/shape/mechanism loop.
Combine task alignment, additive sub-connectivity, and coordinate rotation to test whether an explanation is structurally grounded.
Organize real-data evidence as event input → capacity sweep → spatial/temporal/network interpretation.
Pair search complexity or beta selection with quality metrics and repeated-run spread.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1: the clearest method-interface and group-independence causal map.
Figure 3: the densest link between M1 task alignment, connectivity mechanism, and rotation robustness.
Figure 2: the most complete synthetic comparison surface.
Figure 4: the strongest real-data input-to-mechanism progression.
failure_patterns: One palette is reused for unrelated levels of meaning without a cross-figure color dictionary.
Small panels, pale bands, dense starbars, and 154×154 heatmaps lose readability when reduced or printed in grayscale.
Captions often omit band/box aggregation, colorbar range, sign semantics, units, and representative-selection rationale.
Public visual-source coverage is incomplete, and the automatically listed visualization.ipynb is a mislabeled MP4 rather than a plotting notebook.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper defines group-wise factorization schematically, then advances through synthetic statistics/trajectories/matrices, M1 alignment/sub-connectivity, and mouse spatial-temporal-network evidence while the appendix fills in capacity, matching, permutation, and beta-selection details.
